tour.welcomeBody: Let me give you a quick 30-second tour of Sales Hub. You can skip anytime.
tour.menuBody: The left menu stays collapsed to keep things tidy. Click here to expand or collapse it — hover any icon to see its name.
tour.dashBody: Your home base — your commission this month, quota progress, bonuses and top customers at a glance.
tour.trackerBody: Track points and quota progress — deals and payment activations that count toward your bonuses.
tour.reportBody: Your detailed monthly commissions, what's unlocked vs pending, and your pay stubs.
tour.resellerBody: Track POS activations attributed to external resellers.
tour.revenueBody: Monthly payment-processing revenue per rep and reseller.
tour.resourcesBody: Your shared sales documents — search, browse and download guides and templates. Two featured tools live here too: the Hardware Overview catalog and the Services & Pricing Guide (with a built-in quote builder).
tour.kaizenBody: Try the Kaizen POS demo — a live, streamed point-of-sale you can show prospects.
tour.proposalsBody: Build and send a branded sales proposal from a Zoho Books estimate.
tour.revenueModelerBody: Model the 5-year P&L of a new merchant — SaaS, payments, terminals, hardware and commissions — and compare SaaS tiers. Internal tool: it shows Cluster costs.
tour.creditsBody: Compensation credits for a termination penalty: pick the Zentact merchant and set the amount, the customer completes and signs the agreement online, approval creates the Zoho Books credit note. Monthly report for accounting. Full guide in Resources → Guides Sales Hub.
tour.leadsBody: Leads from the website and phone calls land here for review. Once accepted, a lead goes into Zoho CRM, a Call is created in your name and the customer gets your welcome email. Guide in Resources → Guides Sales Hub.
tour.partnersBody: Manage partner companies and review the opportunities they submit. Approving one creates a Lead in Zoho, assigned to the Cluster rep you pick. The Statistics tab shows the pipeline — volume received, what is still open, won versus lost, and conversion per partner.
tour.adminBody: Admin tools — salespeople, imports, integrations, users, and more.
tour.profileBody: Your account settings, language and preferences.
tour.sofiaBody: Click me anytime for help, or to take this tour again. Enjoy Sales Hub!
tour.askError: Sorry, something went wrong — try again.
tour.hrBody: Prepare a new rep's hiring file: offer and compensation agreement are generated, the candidate signs on screen, then someone signs for Cluster. Salary data — visible only with the HR permissions.
tour.supportBody: High-level reports on Zoho Desk tickets: volume, resolution times, issue types, teams, merchants, and tickets crossed with revenue and churn. What separates merchants who leave is slow tickets, not ticket counts.
tour.passBody: The merchant referral program. The credit is floored when the referral is submitted, capped when the new merchant goes live, then confirmed by hand before accounting is told.
tour.rateCalculatorBody: Drop in the PDF statement of a merchant's current payment processor: you get a comparison with Cluster's pricing, a line-by-line audit of every fee, and two PDFs. "SUSPECT" is the label worth raising — a fee billed under a name with no network counterpart.
tour.icplusRatesBody: The published network rates the IC+ calculator judges statements against. Typed as a percent, stored as a decimal, each one sourced and traced. Published rates only — never a figure read off a statement.
tour.saasIncreaseBody: Apply a SaaS price increase to a subscription. It takes effect at that subscription's own next renewal, never on a shared date.
tour.saasIncreaseLookupBody: The support desk's reference when a merchant calls about their bill: search one account and read back the old price, the new price, the date and the exact notice they received.
tour.openerMatchBody: Every Cluster customer restaurant linked to its Google listing, with its version: V2 (Kaizen) or V1 (Zoho Billing subscribers). Doubtful cases are confirmed here; this is what shows a restaurant as a "customer" on the openers' map.
tour.openerRoutesBody: All door-to-door work in one place. "Campaign & routes": Montreal, Laval, the North Shore and South Shore already split into one-day routes, mapping progress, a finish estimate by number of openers, and one-click "Plan the week"; the Tracking tab confirms each visit by the check-in location. "Field app": the opener's phone app. "Cluster locations": our customers linked to their Google listing.
tour.openerFieldBody: The opener's app, to open on their phone: the day's route on a map, each restaurant's card, check-in, lead creation and the day summary.
tour.moreBody: Every other screen you have access to: sales tools, compensation, operations, administration — plus your profile, theme, language and sign-out. The search at the top jumps straight to any screen.
tour.ndaBody: Send a non-disclosure agreement to another company: Cluster’s mutual NDA (EN or FR) or their own PDF. They sign on screen, then Cluster’s signatory countersigns.
tour.golfBody: Call golf clubs about an alternative to Lightspeed (formerly GGGolf): contact list, call questionnaire, callbacks and meetings.
tour.financeBody: Finance: the CFO’s FY2027 budget. The Master Budget is the income statement; open a line to see its accounts and click one to reach the page that calculates it. Yellow cells on the driver, payroll and OPEX pages are editable and save automatically; approving locks the budget.

terms.title: The Pass program terms
terms.sub: The rules of Cluster's referral program, open to Cluster merchants in Canada.
terms.amountsNote: Current amounts, tiers and perks are published on the program page. They are not repeated here so that a single source governs.

p: The Pass is Cluster's referral program. A member merchant introduces a restaurant to us; if that restaurant becomes an active Cluster customer, the member receives credit on their Cluster account.
The program is offered in Canada only.
Membership is open to active Cluster customers based in Canada. It is held in the business's name, in a commercial context.
One membership per business or group of businesses.
Access works through a link sent to the customer account's email address. That address identifies the member: credit is applied to the matching account.
Cluster may suspend or withdraw a membership in case of misrepresentation, abuse of the program, or unwanted solicitation carried out in its name.
The referred restaurant must be based in Canada and must not already be a Cluster customer.
A member cannot refer themselves, nor a business they control or that belongs to their group.
By submitting a referral, the member confirms they obtained the contact's permission before sharing their details with us.
Cluster determines whether each referral qualifies.

sections.h: 4. One credit per restaurant: first to submit
p: If several members refer the same restaurant, the credit goes to whoever submitted first. Matching is done on the restaurant's name and city.
A referral found not to qualify does not prevent another member from later referring the same restaurant.
The program has tiers. A member's tier depends on how many of their referrals have gone live since they joined; it never moves back down.

The tier that applies to a referral is the one reached BEFORE that referral is counted. In other words, the referral that crosses a tier threshold is paid at the previous tier, and the ones after it at the new tier.
The amount attached to a tier is a MAXIMUM. The exact amount for a referral is confirmed by Cluster based on the services the referred restaurant takes.
Entitlement to the credit arises when the referred restaurant becomes an active customer of Cluster or Cluster Pay. The tier's maximum amount applies when it adopts both.
All amounts are in Canadian dollars.

sections.h: 6. The amount shown at submission is guaranteed
p: The amount of the member's tier at the moment they submit a referral is guaranteed as a MINIMUM for that referral, even if program amounts are later reduced.
If their tier rises between submission and go-live, the higher amount applies.
The credit is applied to the member's Cluster account and offsets their invoices. It is not paid in cash, is not redeemable for cash, and is not transferable to another business.
Cluster issues a credit note and notifies the member.
Once granted, the credit stays with the member. If the referred restaurant later stops being a Cluster customer, the credit is not reclaimed.
Neither a granted credit nor a tier reached expires.
Some tiers unlock further perks, including a discount on Cluster products granted as Cluster credit, promotional items, and a dedicated contact.
These perks are granted on the terms in effect when they are requested. They are not redeemable for cash.

sections.h: 11. Changes to or end of the program
p: Cluster may change the program's amounts, tiers and perks, or end the program, at any time.
Referrals already submitted remain governed by the terms in effect on their submission date, including the guarantee in section 6.
Credit received may have tax or accounting consequences for the member business. It is the member's responsibility to assess and comply with them.
To contact a referred restaurant, Cluster collects the business name, city, province, and the contact's details as provided by the member.
This information is handled in accordance with Cluster's privacy policy.
The member remains responsible for having obtained the contact's permission before sharing their details.
Members choose their correspondence language when they join; program communications are sent in that language.
These terms are maintained in French and in English.
For any question about the program: thepass@clustersystems.com.

why.q: Why is my price going up?
why.a: Cluster invests continuously in the platform: the software, the integrations and the support behind them. The increase sustains that work. For most accounts this is their first increase since they joined — worth mentioning, it defuses a lot of frustration.

howMuch.a: It varies by plan. Look up their account above and read them the New price shown: that is exactly what will be billed, before tax. Never do the math in your head and never guess a percentage.

when.a: At their own subscription's renewal — not a single date for everyone. The exact date is on the record under Takes effect. Nothing is charged before then, and their current invoice is unchanged until it.

notice.a: The badge at the top of the record says so, with the date. If a notice went out, the address used is shown right below it — that is often the explanation for "I never got anything": a billing address that has gone stale.

refuse.q: The customer refuses or threatens to leave
refuse.a: Do not grant a discount, an exception or a reversal. You do not have that authority, and a promise made on the phone is very hard to take back. Listen, log the request, confirm the facts, and escalate. Only a manager can approve an exception.

cancel.a: Under the terms of their existing agreement, which vary by account. Do not play lawyer and do not quote a clause from memory: escalate anything contractual or about termination.

noNotice.a: Check the address on the record. If it is out of date, confirm the new price and the date verbally, take down the correct address and ask an admin to resend. Do not forward the email yourself from your own mailbox.

escalate.a: Any request for a discount or exception, anything contractual, and any case where the figures on the record look wrong to you. Never commit Cluster to a price. Escalate to Samantha Samuels — samantha.samuels@clustersystems.com.

desk.title: Customer Success load
desk.method: No Zoho Desk field says "this ticket is about the price increase", so this compares each notified merchant TO HIMSELF: tickets opened in the N days after his notice versus the N days before it. Same merchant, same length, a few weeks apart. Only merchants whose notice is at least N days old are counted — including yesterday's would truncate the after-window and make the increase look harmless.

why.noNotices: No merchant in this campaign has been notified yet. The comparison needs a notice date to measure from.
why.windowTooLong: {{notified}} merchants were notified, but the earliest notice only went out {{oldest}} — none is yet {{days}} days old, so none has a complete period on BOTH sides. The count above is unaffected; only the before/after comparison needs that distance. Pick a shorter window, or wait.
why.no_name_match: None of the {{merchants}} eligible merchants could be matched to a Zoho Desk account. Matching is by normalised company name, so this usually means Desk holds them under a different name than Billing does.
why.wrong_desk: {{anyDept}} tickets exist from these merchants in the window, but none on the selected desk. They are writing somewhere else — switch the desk above, or pick All desks to see where.

why.no_tickets: {{accounts}} of the {{merchants}} eligible merchants exist in Desk, and none of them has opened a ticket at all. That is a real answer, not a gap: the increase generated no support contact from them.

payments.formula: Each forecast month: churned = active × churn %; active = previous active + installs + conversion adds − churned; fees per merchant grow by the growth %; gross fees = active × fees per merchant; residual = gross fees × processor margin.
payments.noTeams: No team is defined in Admin → Teams: every activation counts as an install.

payments.noSeed: No actual month to start from.
payments.versionHint: Saves the forecast months as they are now, to compare them with the actuals later.

payments.definitions: Active = merchants with at least one transaction or fee in the month. Churned = active the previous month, no activity this month (Zentact does not date closures). Installs = activations outside the conversion team. Residual = transaction profit + other revenue (Cluster's margin). Amounts in CAD.

lev.title: Levers
lev.sub: Exact effects computed from the FY{{fy}} model. Each lever moves one thing and keeps the other unchanged.
lev.growth: +1 point of growth = +{{amt}} of revenue (1 % of last year's revenue).
lev.margin: {{amt}} less OPEX = +1 point of margin (1 % of this year's revenue), revenue unchanged.
lev.gapGrowth: To close the {{pts}} gap with growth alone: +{{amt}} of extra revenue.
lev.gapCost: To close the {{pts}} gap with costs alone: {{amt}} less OPEX ({{pct}} of OPEX).
lev.ok: The model is at or above 40: no effort needed to reach the threshold.
lev.unknown: The score cannot be computed (no revenue base).
lev.whatIf: What if OPEX were lower by

shippedNote.rule_of_40_aleph2026_median: 342 companies, 110 reporting the metric; revenue growth plus profit margin, EBITDA margin most common.
shippedNote.rule_of_40_aleph2026_top_quartile: Aspirational level, shown but not used to flag areas to improve.
shippedNote.gross_margin_aleph2026_blended: Blended margin including services and other revenue. A POS company selling hardware and payments is structurally lower: read as a distance to pure SaaS, not as a target.
shippedNote.gross_margin_aleph2026_software: Software revenue only; our model margin covers all revenue, so this one is informational.
shippedNote.gross_margin_toast_fy2024: Derived by Sales Hub from the filing: revenue 4,960 M USD less total costs of revenue 3,770 M USD, rounded. Payments revenue is reported gross, so it is not comparable with a net-revenue presentation.
shippedNote.arr_per_location_toast_fy2024: Derived by Sales Hub: ARR 1,626 M USD divided by about 134,000 locations. Toast ARR includes a payments component; our figure is in CAD.
shippedNote.nrr_aleph2026_median: 230 companies reporting. The model has no net retention figure (no expansion data): shown for reference.
shippedNote.grr_aleph2026_median: 226 companies reporting; down from 88 in 2024. Our annual logo churn is the closest model figure (1 minus churn).
shippedNote.cac_payback_months_aleph2026_median: 198 companies reporting. S&M expense divided by (new ARR times gross margin), times 12.
shippedNote.ltv_cac_aleph2026_median: 146 companies reporting. CLTV = annual revenue per customer times gross margin divided by annual churn; CAC = total S&M divided by new customers.
shippedNote.rd_pct_aleph2026_median: 192 companies reporting; quartiles 10 % to 40 %. Spending above a benchmark is a question to ask, not necessarily a problem.
shippedNote.sm_pct_aleph2026_median: Quoted on the R&D page of the report; the page does not label it explicitly as a median.
shippedNote.ga_pct_aleph2026: Quoted on the R&D page of the report; the page does not label it explicitly as a median.
shippedNote.rd_pct_saascap2026_median: Percent of ARR, not of revenue; over 1,000 respondents. Informational.
shippedNote.sm_pct_saascap2026: Sum of two separate medians (sales 15 %, marketing 8 %); medians do not strictly add. Percent of ARR. Informational.
shippedNote.ga_pct_saascap2026_median: Percent of ARR, not of revenue. Informational.
